params.script_inline:
import sys, json

# The DECLARATION of this memory's own tool, in the hive, beside the cells that
# serve it.
#
# WHY IT LIVES HERE. Whoever is reached declares themselves. Until GH #552 this
# schema was a HAND-TYPED projection of THIS hive's own `in_query` contract,
# kept in a collector one composite away: `memory-hive` named seven context keys
# on that lane, three of them were the model's, and a person had retyped those
# three -- twice, because `talky`'s brain seeded a second copy -- into templates
# that answer no recall at all. Nothing but a test held the copies to the
# contract, and a schema held to its contract by a test is a schema that has no
# owner.
#
# The lane pair and the answer shape are the tools hive's, byte for byte
# (`templates/tools/README.md` § Asking for the declarations): a caller that can
# ask one answerer can ask the other, and the collector cuts three answers
# together without knowing which of them was a hive of tools.
#
# THE DESCRIPTION IS WHERE THE RULES ARE WRITTEN. `read_window` in `./recall`
# REFUSES a half-open window (`half_open_window`) rather than widening it, and
# until this cell existed that rule was enforced in one template and unsaid in
# another -- a model that named one bound bought a refusal it could not see
# coming. It is one sentence now, in the file that enforces it.
#
# THE TIER IS NOT AN ARGUMENT and never becomes one. How deep a recall runs is
# configuration of this hive (`./tool` params.tier); a model that could choose
# its own depth could ask for one the instance was tuned away from.
SCHEMAS = {
    "memory_recall": {
        "description":
            "Ask this member's long-term memory about something, optionally "
            "restricted to a time range. Name BOTH bounds or neither: a "
            "half-open window is refused, not widened.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "query": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "what to look for"},
                "window_from": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "ISO-8601 start of the time range "
                                   "(optional; needs `window_to`)"},
                "window_to": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "ISO-8601 end of the time range "
                                   "(optional; needs `window_from`)"}},
            "required": ["query"]}}
}

# THE SIDECAR SECTION THIS MEMORY OFFERS (GH #606). The same rule as the schema
# above, read one word wider: whoever is REACHED declares themselves. The block
# a `splitter` cuts out of an answer is composed by an asking collector, and
# what goes in it is offered by whoever reads it -- so the rules of the memory
# section live in the hive that ingests it, beside `extract-glue` and
# `predicate-core.json`, and not as a literal in a collector one composite away.
#
# `templates/memory-hive/inline-contract.md` stays the AUTHORITY: this is the
# copy that reaches a model, the file is where the reasoning behind every line
# of it is written down, and a drift lock asserts the two are one text.
#
# THE FENCE IS NOT NAMED HERE, and that is the whole shape of #606. Until it,
# this text opened by telling a model to write ```memory: one section, one
# fence, one consumer. The collector owns the frame now -- ONE ```sidecar block
# with one key per section -- so a second consumer of the same fence costs an
# offer rather than a second block, and this text says only what belongs under
# the key `memory`.
#
# The SCHEMA is the shape, the INSTRUCTION is the discipline, and the collector
# renders the example out of the schema: every property named in `required` is
# shown, which is why `nothing_new` is not one -- printed on every content
# block it would read as a field that has to be got right on the turns where it
# means nothing, and the empty form the ingress actually parses is shown by the
# instruction instead.
MEMORY_RULES = """ANNOTATE EVERY TURN, including the turns that changed nothing. This section has both parts -- `facts`, this turn's delta of world state, and `topic`, where the conversation stands.

experience = what happened between us, foresight = expected or planned.
start opens a thread, end closes it by name, continue is ordinary.

A turn that carried nothing is still ANNOTATED; leaving the section out is a fault:
{"memory":{"nothing_new":true,"facts":[],"topic":{"movement":"continue"}}}

DELTA, NOT STATE: what the memory handed you is already remembered; say what this turn
CHANGED. Your own answer is not a fact, and a question asserts nothing about what it asks.

PREDICATES ARE KEYS: English, snake_case -- one relation, one key, in every language.
single (one at a time; a later replaces it): born_on, diet, favorite_color,
favorite_food, favorite_music, job_title, lives_in, partner_of, preferred_language,
pronouns, relationship_status, timezone, works_at
multi (the axis ENUMERATES; values coexist): allergic_to, dislikes, friend_of, has_child,
has_parent, has_pet, has_sibling, likes, lived_in, member_of, owns, skilled_in,
speaks_language, studied_at, visited, worked_at
A PREDICATE NAMES THE SUBJECT MATTER, NEVER THE SPEECH ACT: an intention is
`fact_kind: foresight` on the matter -- `lives_in`, never `wants_to_move_to`.

ENTITIES ARE VERBATIM: names and values are copied byte for byte, never translated or
corrected."""

MEMORY_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "facts": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "subject": {"type": "string"},
                    "predicate": {"type": "string"},
                    "claim": {"type": "string"},
                    "fact_kind": {"type": "string",
                                  "enum": ["world", "experience", "foresight"]},
                    "valid_from": {"type": "string",
                                   "description": "<RFC3339|null>"}},
                "required": ["subject", "predicate", "claim", "fact_kind",
                             "valid_from"]}},
        "topic": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "movement": {"type": "string",
                             "enum": ["start", "continue", "end"]},
                "name": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["movement", "name"]},
        "nothing_new": {
            "type": "boolean",
            "description": "true on the empty form and absent otherwise"}},
    "required": ["facts", "topic"]}

# REQUIRED, and it is the obligation of GH #299 in one field: a turn nobody
# annotated is a turn nobody extracts, so an absent section is a fault and not a
# modest answer. The offer travels on EVERY answer of this cell, including the
# one that found no tool name it serves -- the section is not a response to a
# name, it is what this hive asks of whoever talks to it.
SIDECAR = [{"section": "memory", "required": True,
            "schema": MEMORY_SCHEMA, "instruction": MEMORY_RULES}]

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
body = doc["body"]
asked = body.get("tools")

# ABSENT and EMPTY are two different requests and must not look alike -- the
# same rule the tools hive follows. A caller that declared no tools gets no
# schemas, and that is an answer; a request that carries no `tools` slot at all
# lost it on the way.
if not isinstance(asked, list):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "schemas", "error_code": "tools_missing",
                   "schema_count": 0, "unknown_count": 0},
        "schemas": [], "unknown": [], "sidecar": SIDECAR,
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": "the request carried no `tools` list"}]}))
    sys.exit(0)

names = [str(n) for n in asked if isinstance(n, str)]
if "*" in names:
    wanted, unknown = sorted(SCHEMAS), []
else:
    seen, wanted, unknown = set(), [], []
    for n in names:
        if n in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(n)
        (wanted if n in SCHEMAS else unknown).append(n)

schemas = [dict(name=n, **SCHEMAS[n]) for n in wanted]
header = {"operation": "schemas", "schema_count": len(schemas),
          "unknown_count": len(unknown)}
if unknown:
    # Named, never dropped: a caller asking this memory for a name it does not
    # serve has to learn that from the answer and not from a silence.
    header["error_code"] = "tool_unknown"
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": header, "schemas": schemas, "unknown": unknown,
    "sidecar": SIDECAR, "messages": []}))

description.purpose: The declaration of this memory's OWN tool, handed out by name: a request naming `memory_recall` comes back as its JSON schema, and any other name comes back in `unknown` rather than as a silence. Whoever is reached declares themselves -- until GH #552 this schema was a HAND-TYPED projection of this hive's own `in_query` contract, living in a collector one composite away and seeded a second time into a brain, held to the contract by nothing but a test. Since GH #606 the same answer also carries `sidecar[]`: what this memory asks for IN RETURN, the section `memory` of the sidecar block -- required, with the schema of the annotation object and the rules of `inline-contract.md` as its instruction. Whoever is reached declares themselves, read one word wider: `collector/assemble` held that text as a literal until #606, one composite away, in a cell that enforces none of its rules.
description.use_when: Reached on this hive's `in_schemas` lane, on an asking collector's menu tick, with the names that collector declares it uses. Never addressed by name, never part of a tool round: it answers no `tool_call` and carries no `tool_name`.
description.not_in_scope: No judgement about which tier a caller SHOULD ask for -- the tier is this hive's configuration (`./tool` params.tier) and deliberately not a model argument, because a model that could choose its own depth could ask for one the instance was tuned away from. No `thread_recall`: that one reads the COLLECTOR's own slate, which no other cell may read, so it is declared where it is answered. No provider envelope: the answer is {name, description, parameters}, and wrapping it in whatever a model provider wants is the caller's business. And no FENCE: the offer says what belongs under the key `memory`, never how many blocks an answer carries or what they open with -- that frame belongs to the collector that composes every section into one contract (GH #606).
description.emits_meaning: schemas[]: `{name, description, parameters}` for every asked name this hive serves, sorted for `*`. unknown[]: the names it does not serve, verbatim. hop.error_code `tool_unknown` when that list is non-empty, `tools_missing` when the request carried no `tools` slot at all -- an absent list and an empty one are two different requests. sidecar[]: the sections this hive asks a model for, `{section, required, schema, instruction}` -- exactly one, `memory`, required. It travels on EVERY answer of this cell, the `tools_missing` one included: a section is not a response to a name. The asking collector merges the offers of all its answerers into one block contract; the fence is stated by that collector's preamble and NOT here.
description.consumes_meaning: body.tools: the names the asking collector declares it uses, e.g. ["memory_recall"]. The single entry ["*"] asks for everything this memory declares, which is one schema.
examples: {"tools":["memory_recall","web_search"]} -> one schema, unknown ["web_search"], hop.error_code `tool_unknown` -- the tools hive answers that one
every answer, whatever was asked -> sidecar[] with one offer, section `memory`, required
